translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition: for every set K of arithmetic sentences, either there is no recursively enumerable set F of arithmetic axioms whose set of derivable sentences is exactly K, or there exists an arithmetic sentence σ that is Π₁ in the library’s syntactic sense, is true in the standard natural numbers, and satisfies both σ ∉ K and ∼σ ∉ K, where ∼σ is its formal negation. The witness σ may depend on K; none is required if the first disjunct holds. There is no assumption that K is sound or consistent, or that F extends any particular base theory.

divergences.description: The target quantifies over every K without assuming Def3 K, which expresses the source’s premise K ⊆ T. Def2 σ requires only the witness to be true. For example, take K to be all arithmetic sentences: K is the theorem set of the recursively enumerable axiom set {⊥}, so the first disjunct is false, and no σ lies outside K, so the second is false too.

Def10 σ restricts the witness to syntactically Π₁ sentences, whereas Koellner’s displayed Claim 3 places no complexity restriction on φ. This is the advertised strengthening motivated by Gödel’s Diophantine wording, not a literal requirement that σ be written as a Diophantine problem.

judgement.summary: The disjunction has the intended shape, but the target is false for some K excluded by the source’s soundness premise. The intended statement needs `∀ K : Def1, Def3 K → ...`.
